Scaleway.summary_note: Scaleway is the highest-scoring provider on EU sovereignty criteria in this survey. As a French SAS wholly owned by Xavier Niel via NJJ Holding (private, no public float since 2021), it has clean legal independence from all non-EU extraterritorial law: no US parent, no CLOUD Act exposure, confirmed in published documentation and validated by France's decision to migrate its National Health Data Hub from Microsoft Azure to Scaleway (2026). The European Commission's selection of Scaleway for the Cloud III DPS at SEAL-3 (Digital Resilience) is the strongest external validation of its sovereignty posture. Scaleway is uniquely differentiated on supply-chain sovereignty by manufacturing its own ARM servers in France and launching the world's first RISC-V cloud servers (2024). It offers a full KMS/BYOK service — rare among European providers — enabling genuine customer cryptographic control. Environmental performance is exceptional: 100% renewable energy since 2017, PUE 1.37 average, WUE near zero, 15,000 servers reconditioned annually, annual Impact Report with ADEME-certified methodology, and real-time customer footprint calculator. Key limitations: BSI C5 not held (French provider, ANSSI/SecNumCloud is the relevant standard, in progress); proprietary control plane is not open-source; NVIDIA GPU dependency for AI workloads remains a non-EU supply-chain constraint; HPC processors are Intel/AMD (N on SOV-6 Q4 as for all providers). The financing of the 2021 Iliad privatisation involved non-EU banks (JPMorgan, BNP bridge loans), a minor SOV-1 note that does not affect ownership or control.
